Fig. 8
Spline plots for the associations of 24 hour urinary sodium and potassium excretion and sodium to- potassium ratio with cardiovascular
risk. The spline analysis of pooled data supported a linear association over the range of sodium excretion (Panel A; 5th to 95th percentile, 1846–
5520 mg) and potassium excretion (Panel B; 5th to 95th percentile, 1462–3961 mg) within the overall study population. The sodium-to-potassium
ratio (Panel C) was assessed on the basis of the sodium and potassium excretion measured in millimoles. Hazard ratios were estimated from Cox
models stratiﬁed according to study cohort with adjustment for age, sex, race, educational level, height, body-mass index, alcohol consumption,
smoking status, physical activity, history of diabetes and elevated cholesterol status, family history of cardiovascular disease, and mutual adjustment
for 24 h urinary potassium and sodium excretions. Shaded areas indicate 95% conﬁdence intervals, and the dashed line at 1.0 indicates the
reference. Box plots at the bottom of the graphs show the distributions of the urinary biomarker. The vertical bar indicates the median, and the ends
of the box the interquartile range; the whiskers (dashed lines) extend to values no farther than 1.5 times the interquartile range (which may be past
the graphed area), and dots indicate values that are farther than 1.5 times the interquartile range.
